title: The Twelve-Year-Old Behind the Register
content: My father ran a hardware store on Main Street in Pawtucket. From twelve on, I worked the register after school. And I noticed things. The contractors cleared out the rock salt two days before the forecast caught up. One brand of cordless drill kept leaving the shelf faster than the rest, even though it cost more. So I took my store wages and bought a few shares of the company that made it. It went up tenfold. But what hooked me wasn't the money. I wanted to know WHY.
extended_content: Those afternoons changed everything. People would tell you what they came in for—'just grabbing a couple of hinges'—and walk out with a cart full of something else. What they said and what they bought were two different datasets, and the second one was the honest one. Nobody advertised that drill. Nobody wrote it up anywhere. The guys who used drills every day just kept coming back for it. I didn't know anything about the company. The return was partly luck. But the noticing wasn't. That feeling of seeing something in plain sight before anyone else wrote it down? I've been chasing it ever since.
when_to_tell: when someone asks how I got started or what sparked my interest
lesson: What people actually do tells you more than what they say.
